growth_story.headline: Tourism lifted Cabo Verde fast, the 2008 crisis and the pandemic knocked it back, and income per person is now at a new high.
growth_story.arc: Income per person in Cabo Verde grew 8.4 percent a year in 1990–2000, as foreign money for tourism, aid and remittances flowed in and market reforms began in 1992. Growth stayed strong at 6.0 percent a year in 2001–2008. The 2008 global crisis cut tourism and investment from Europe, and growth fell to 1.2 percent a year in 2009–2016, even as borrowed money paid for public building and public debt climbed. Growth came back at 3.6 percent a year in 2017–2025, led by tourism, despite a 20.9 percent fall in income per person in 2020 when the pandemic stopped travel. Income per person reached a new high in 2025, but growth swings more from year to year than in most economies.

threads.title: Tourism, aid and remittances
threads.text: From the early 1990s, foreign money for tourism hotels, aid, money sent home by emigrants and public spending on infrastructure drove fast growth. Market reforms, including the sale of state firms, began in 1992. Income per person more than doubled between 1990 and 2000.

threads.title: The 2008 shock and rising debt
threads.text: The 2008 global crisis hit tourism and investment from Europe. The government borrowed to build energy, road, airport and port projects and to support loss-making state firms, but growth stayed weak while public debt climbed.

threads.title: Pandemic collapse and rebound
threads.text: Covid-19 shut down tourism in 2020, and income per person fell 20.9 percent, the deepest drop in the record. It bounced back by 15.2 percent in 2022 and passed its 2019 level in 2023.

citations.title: Cabo Verde Economic Update: Rebounding from the Crisis

citations.title: Cabo Verde Economic Update: Rebounding from the Crisis
citations.quote: Driven by the shutdown in the tourism sector, GDP contracted by 14.8 percent in 2020 (15.7 percent in per-capita terms)

threads.title: Tourism on two islands
threads.text: Tourism is still the main engine, with record arrivals in 2025 and arrivals still rising in early 2026. Most of it sits on two islands, Sal and Boa Vista.

threads.text: Public debt is falling but remains high. Debts of state firms, mostly in aviation, add risk to the budget.

since_last_year.text: Growth stayed strong through 2025, when income per person rose 5.8 percent, and carried into early 2026 on tourism and investment. Public debt kept falling, and inflation eased after fuel prices were capped.

citations.title: Macro Poverty Outlook: Cabo Verde (October 2026)
citations.quote: Growth momentum from 2025 has carried into 2026, with real GDP expanding 6.4 percent in Q1 (year-on-year, y/y), driven by tourism and investment.

citations.title: Macro Poverty Outlook: Cabo Verde (October 2026)
citations.quote: Public debt is projected to reach 93.9 percent of GDP by end-2026, down from 99.9 percent in 2025.

citations.title: Macro Poverty Outlook: Cabo Verde (October 2026)
citations.quote: Inflationary pressures eased markedly: inflation fell to 0.4 percent in July 2026 y/y, from 2.7 percent a year earlier, reflecting caps on fuel prices

growth_story.tension: The World Bank's April 2021 account of the pandemic year records a smaller drop in income per person than the data file, which now shows a fall of 20.9 percent in 2020.
